question: What is the difference between `vector`, `deque`, and `list`?

scenes.sub: One block, a set of chunks, or a chain of nodes.
scenes.say: Vector, deque, and list. Three sequence containers. The difference comes down to how they lay out memory.

scenes.head: Same six numbers, three layouts
scenes.say: A vector keeps them in one contiguous block. A deque keeps fixed size chunks, plus a small index of pointers to them. Adding at either end just fills a chunk, or adds a new one. Nothing shifts. A list gives every element its own node, somewhere on the heap, linked to its neighbors by previous and next pointers. Inserting in the middle just relinks pointers. But walking a list means jumping all over memory.

scenes.head: Side by side
scenes.say: Random access: vector and deque are O of one, a list has to walk. Back operations: fast for all three. Front: vector has to shift everything, deque and list don't. Middle inserts: only list is O of one, if you already have an iterator there. Memory: vector is the tightest, list pays two extra pointers per element. And cache use: vector is the best by far, which is why it often beats list in practice, even for middle inserts.

scenes.head: So which one?

panels.code:
std::vector<int> v;  // default choice
std::deque<int>  q;  // fast at both ends: queues, sliding windows
std::list<int>   l;  // stable iterators, O(1) splice and insert

std::list<int> other = {7, 8};
l.splice(l.begin(), other);  // moves nodes, copies nothing

scenes.say: So which one? Vector by default. It's the fastest in practice, and what the C plus plus Core Guidelines recommend. Deque when you push and pop at both ends, like a queue or a sliding window. It's also the default container behind the queue and stack adaptors. List when you need iterators that stay valid while other elements come and go, or splice: moving nodes between lists without copying a single element.

lines: vector: one contiguous block. Fast access, fast at the back, cache-friendly.
deque: chunks. O(1) at both ends, still random access. list: nodes, O(1) splice.
Default to vector. Measure before picking list.
scenes.say: Vector is one contiguous block, fast and cache friendly. Deque is chunks, fast at both ends. List is linked nodes, with cheap inserts and splices, but slow to walk. Default to vector, and measure before you pick a list.
